description: Canonical digest suite vocabulary for v1 typed digest values. A digest suite is the registered tuple (canonicalization, hash_algorithm). The suite canonical_id is the wire prefix in `<suite>:<lowercase_hex>` typed digest values and the value space of the Realm `digest_algorithm` field.
suite_id_grammar: suite_id = hash_id | canonicalization_id '.' hash_id ; each segment matches [a-z0-9_]+ ; at most one dot. A bare hash_id (no dot) denotes canonicalization=json_jcs for historical wire compatibility.
registry_rules: A digest suite id without a dot denotes canonicalization=json_jcs (canonical JSON per zh/conformance/encoding.md §2). The bare ids sha256/blake3 are therefore JSON-canonicalization suites; their wire semantics are unchanged from earlier v1 drafts and existing signed bytes are unaffected.

Suites are registered as explicit tuples. Implementations MUST NOT combine canonicalization ids and hash ids freely; only suites present as rows in this registry exist, and only status=active rows are valid on wire.

A suite prefix not present as an active row MUST fail closed with unsupported_digest_algorithm when it appears in a critical field (event_digest, state_root, prev_refs / refs digest, seal id, receipt digest); in non-critical metadata receivers MAY record it as unknown and preserve raw bytes (zh/conformance/encoding.md §3.2).
status=reserved rows pin the wire prefix and profile gate but MUST NOT appear on wire until every activation_requirements entry is met and the row is flipped to active in a registry release.

Every status=active row MUST declare kat_vector_id naming an active vector-registry entry; every status=reserved row MUST instead declare kat_absence_reason and MUST NOT declare kat_vector_id. tools/lint_artifacts.py enforces this binding.

Realm digest_algorithm MUST hold exactly one active suite id; every digest produced inside that Realm MUST use the declared suite. A digest whose suite prefix differs from the Realm's declared suite MUST be rejected (schema_violation), except on a Transition Seal's previous_state_root. Suite transition only via ak.profile.hash_transition.v1 (zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §9.3.2).

Schema enum values for digest-suite selector fields (e.g. realm.digest_algorithm) MUST be generated from active rows' canonical_id only when publishing a new schema version, then frozen for that schema version. Activating a reserved/new suite requires a new schema version and profile negotiation; registry activation MUST NOT expand an existing schema enum in place (zh/conformance/schema-registry.md §6.1 b.1).

The hash_strength_order below is consumed by the suite-transition no-downgrade rule and applies to the hash_algorithm component only; canonicalization component changes are lateral and carry no strength relation.

The registry is intentionally minimal: new hash algorithms (e.g. SHA-3 family for algorithm diversity, post-quantum hash families) and new canonicalizations enter additively as new rows with their own profile gates and conformance vectors; the <suite>:<hex> wire form needs no rewrite. KDF/ciphersuite algorithm selectors elsewhere in the spec (e.g. key-backup PBKDF2 digest_algorithm, VOPRF SHA-512) are separate value spaces and are NOT digest suites.

hash_strength_order.note: Performance-side order; v1 treats registered hashes as equal collision strength. Extended when post-quantum or diversity hashes are registered.

canonicalizations.definition: Arkret canonical JSON (RFC 8785 / JCS narrowed profile), zh/conformance/encoding.md §2.
canonicalizations.notes: Implied by bare (dot-free) suite ids; never written as an explicit dotted prefix segment in v1.

canonicalizations.definition: CBOR deterministic encoding (RFC 8949 §4.2) under the Arkret profile to be pinned by ak.profile.encoding.cbor.v1 (encoding rules, CDDL, schema-agnostic JSON<->CBOR type mapping, conformance vectors).
canonicalizations.notes: Reserved until ak.profile.encoding.cbor.v1 is fully specified. The mapping MUST be schema-agnostic (JSON string -> CBOR text string, JSON integer -> CBOR integer); canonicalization MUST NOT depend on schema knowledge.

suites.security_note: v1 default; all receivers MUST support. SHA-2 family, not post-quantum but Grover-degraded strength remains acceptable; migration path via suite transition.
Best throughput (parallelizable); recommended for blob CID and high-volume paths.

suites.kat_absence_reason: Deterministic CBOR encoding and per-suite digest vectors are not published until all activation_requirements are complete.
activation_requirements: ak.profile.encoding.cbor.v1 fully specified: deterministic encoding rules pinned by directly adopting an upstream standardized deterministic CBOR profile (CDE, draft-ietf-cbor-cde, or dCBOR, draft-mcnally-deterministic-cbor) under draft-pinning discipline (draft change = new profile version) rather than a bespoke ruleset, CDDL for envelope and canonical objects, schema-agnostic JSON<->CBOR type mapping
Per-suite conformance vectors published (canonical bytes, event_digest, state_root, receipt digest)
Suite transition vectors published for json_jcs -> cbor transition Seals
suites.security_note: Deterministic CBOR canonicalization with SHA-256. Same hash strength as sha256; the suite exists to enable encode-once/sign-the-bytes verification and MLS/COSE ecosystem alignment for Realms that opt in at create time.
